description: Provides access to the device's pixel density and font scale, and helps calculate pixel-perfect sizes for images, layouts, and fonts.

get.description: Returns the device pixel density (DPI ratio).
get.returns: Device pixel density as a number (e.g., 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 3.5)
examples: PixelRatio.get() === 2 // iPhone SE, iPhone XR, xhdpi Android devices
PixelRatio.get() === 3 // iPhone X, XS, XS Max, xxhdpi Android devices

getFontScale.description: Returns the font scale factor applied by the user.
getFontScale.returns: Scaling factor for fonts; defaults to device pixel ratio if not set.
notes: On Android: reflects Settings > Display > Font size
On iOS: reflects Settings > Display & Brightness > Text Size or Accessibility > Larger Text

getPixelSizeForLayoutSize.description: Converts a layout size in dp to a pixel size in px, guaranteed to return an integer.

roundToNearestPixel.description: Rounds a layout size to the nearest layout size that corresponds to an integer number of pixels.
roundToNearestPixel.example: PixelRatio.roundToNearestPixel(8.4) // returns 8.33 on a device with PixelRatio 3

usage_tips: Use getPixelSizeForLayoutSize when fetching higher resolution images for high-density devices.
Use roundToNearestPixel to avoid blurry borders or layout issues due to fractional pixels.
PixelRatio.getFontScale is useful when doing custom font calculations that respect user settings.
